assessment.nobel_worthiness: Random-coefficients demand estimation with endogenous prices (BLP) and the Ericson-Pakes dynamic industry framework changed how demand, market power, mergers and welfare are measured. The methods are standard in antitrust, regulation and applied IO, and their influence on empirical work is broad and lasting.
assessment.attribution: The BLP core (Berry, Levinsohn, Pakes) is clearly identifiable. Bresnahan, Reiss, Benkard and Levin made important adjacent contributions, so a three-name limit excludes deserving people, but the BLP trio is the most defensible core.
assessment.maturity: Three decades of use across fields, with extensive replication, refinement and practical adoption. Timing is not a concern.
uncertainties: Whether the committee prefers to include Bresnahan for his earlier contributions to empirical IO
Whether the IO/econometric methods framing is judged sufficiently distinct from earlier awards in empirical methods

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The heterogeneous-firm model moved trade theory from industry-level to firm-level analysis. It explains exporter selection, within-industry reallocation and a new channel for gains from trade. It also reshaped empirical trade work and policy evaluation.
assessment.attribution: Melitz (2003) is the central contribution, and Helpman's work on monopolistic competition, multinationals and heterogeneous firms is a long, foundational body of work. Redding is influential but later and more quantitative. The pairing is a clean credit assignment.
assessment.maturity: More than two decades of confirmation with broad empirical support and wide adoption. The Krugman award in 2008 does not preempt this firm-level extension.
uncertainties: Overlap with the Helpman-Grossman candidate and the Ricardian quantitative trade candidate may split support
Some empirical evidence challenges particular parametric assumptions, though not the core insight

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The New Keynesian framework, with nominal rigidities, microfoundations and rule-based monetary policy, underlies modern central bank analysis. Its policy influence on inflation targeting and the Taylor-rule tradition is very large.
assessment.attribution: The credit is spread widely: Calvo and Taylor on staggered pricing and contracts, Woodford and Gali on the canonical synthesis, Christiano, Eichenbaum and Smets on estimated DSGE models. Any three-name set is contestable, so attribution is the main weakness.
assessment.maturity: Mature and heavily used in policy for more than 25 years. The inflation episode after 2021 produced debate but also further validation and extension.
uncertainties: Hard to choose a three-person subset from a large pool
Post-2021 inflation raised questions about how well the baseline model performs
Gertler appears on two ballots, and the framework's relationship to prior macro prizes may matter

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Kiyotaki and Moore's credit-cycles model shows how collateral values and borrowing constraints amplify and propagate shocks. It is foundational for macro-finance, financial-crisis analysis and the later financial-accelerator literature.
assessment.attribution: The 1997 paper is a clear and well-defined origin of the collateral-constraint mechanism. Gertler and Gilchrist are important for the financial accelerator and empirical development, but the core pair is distinct.
assessment.maturity: A long record of influence, strongly reinforced by the 2008 crisis and later work. The topic is partly adjacent to the 2022 banking-crisis prize but is a different mechanism.
uncertainties: The committee may see the Bernanke-Gertler-Gilchrist line as the competing framing
Partial overlap with the 2022 prize topic

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Rubinstein's alternating-offers model gave bargaining a tractable strategic foundation, and the Rubinstein-Wolinsky work connected bargaining to decentralized markets and search. These are core building blocks in game theory, labour and monetary search models, and matching markets.
assessment.attribution: Rubinstein (1982) is the decisive contribution, and Wolinsky is the natural co-credit through the market-bargaining extension. Binmore's contributions were important but more supportive and partly parallel.
assessment.maturity: A classic, extensively used for over 40 years. The long delay raises only a mild question of whether the committee considers the area already honoured through earlier game-theory prizes.
uncertainties: Earlier game-theory prizes may reduce urgency
Rubinstein's later behavioural and critical work might shape how the committee frames the citation

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The task-based view of technology and the China-shock studies changed understanding of how automation and trade reshape labour demand, wages and local labour markets. The impact on research and public policy debate is exceptionally large.
assessment.attribution: Autor is the central figure, with Hanson and Dorn as co-authors of the trade-shock work. Katz's earlier work on skill-biased change and the task-model contributions from others such as Acemoglu complicate credit.
assessment.maturity: Fairly mature, with extensive follow-up. Some findings on the persistence and magnitude of effects are still being refined, and parts of the literature are contested.
uncertainties: Overlap with others working on technology and inequality, including contributions credited outside this ballot entry
Debate over the size and generality of the China-shock estimates

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Collective and bargaining models of the household replaced the unitary model and made intrahousehold allocation testable. They matter for welfare analysis, labour supply, policy design and development.
assessment.attribution: Chiappori's collective model with testable restrictions is the clearest contribution. Pollak is credited for bargaining and separate-spheres models, and Lundberg for empirical and bargaining work. Other pioneers such as Manser-Brown, McElroy-Horney and Browning are outside the credited names, so attribution is incomplete.
assessment.maturity: Mature, with decades of empirical testing and widespread adoption in family and development economics.
uncertainties: Priority disputes among pioneers of household bargaining models
Possible view that the field is more specialised than the top candidates

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Bayesian persuasion and information design give a general framework for how a sender can optimally shape what others learn. It is an elegant, tractable approach with applications to mechanism design, markets, regulation and communication, and it connects to the committee's tradition of information economics and design.
assessment.attribution: Kamenica-Gentzkow (2011) is the origin, while Bergemann-Morris developed the information-design and robust-predictions agenda in parallel. Choosing three of four credited names is difficult, and Gentzkow's other major work is in empirical media economics.
assessment.maturity: Less mature than the other top candidates. The framework is about 15 years old and still developing, with applications that are growing but not yet deeply confirmed in empirical practice.
uncertainties: Possibly premature relative to older candidates
Attribution among Kamenica, Gentzkow, Bergemann and Morris is uncertain
Limited empirical or policy implementation so far
